title: Token ingest lightweight fastlane + hint cache to cut prefill overhead
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Prefill-side preprocessing (tokenization + normalization + session lookup) contributes a disproportionate share of end-to-end prefill latency and CPU cost for short prompts and high-concurrency workloads. Current pipeline does full Unicode normalization, heavy token hashing, and kernel-selection metadata enrichment on every request, which increases tail latency and GC pressure for hot shards.

Goal: Implement a lightweight "fastlane" for token ingest that detects common low-cost inputs (ascii/simple-whitespace prompts, repeated session prefixes) and routes them through a shallow, vectorized path that: 1) skips costly Unicode normalization, 2) uses a small LRU/TTL hint cache keyed by session+prefix fingerprint, and 3) attaches compact kernel-hint metadata to the prefill request so downstream schedulers and kernel selectors can avoid unnecessary kernel probing. Target metrics: reduce CPU cycles per prefill for common-case by ~35%, 95th prefill latency down 10-20ms on small prompts, and overall tokenization cost savings ~12% on our default production mix.

Approach:
- Fastlane detection layer in ingress: cheap checks (ASCII-only, length thresholds, token-boundary heuristics) implemented as branchless SIMD-friendly checks to avoid branching overhead.
- Hint cache: session-scoped LRU with a small footprint (configurable 128 entries by default) that stores: normalized prefix digest, tokenized prefix length, and kernel-hint tuple (preferred kernel family + quantization profile). TTL default 60s, but adaptive eviction when memory pressure detected.
- Minimal tokenization bailouts: if fastlane detection fails, fall back to full pipeline; metrics recorded for each bailout reason.
- Kernel hint propagation: fastlane attaches compact metadata to the prefill RPC (enum-coded) so the kernel selection component can skip full model kernel probing and use the hinted kernel family. Backward compatible: if downstream component does not recognize hints, it ignores them.

Outcomes & constraints:
- Must preserve exact tokenization semantics for non-fastlane paths. Fastlane will provide probabilistic equivalence for ASCII-only inputs; all fastlane outputs include a checksum so we can detect divergence and trigger revert-to-full-pipeline on the same request.
- Memory budget for hint cache must be tunable per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private). Private deployments can set cache=0.
- Maintain auditability: all fastlane metadata and bailout reasons are logged to the Console under a low-cost aggregation bucket for 7 days by default.

Compatibility: integrates with Dedicated autopool and Private runtime; shipping will include a feature flag (runtime.ingest_fastlane) and an opt-out header for customers who require deterministic full-tokenization on every request.
comments: 2026-02-22: Initial spike completed. Prototype microbench with 50k mixed prompts shows 32% CPU reduction for ascii-dominant traffic. Prototype located in runtime/ingest/fastlane-spike branch.

2026-02-27: Design review with ML infra and kernel team. Decided to keep hint payload minimal (1 byte enum + 16-bit prefix length) to avoid RPC bloat. Action: Marco to add analytics tags and failure counters.

2026-03-05: Implementation PR opened (see attachments). Unit tests for ASCII fastlane and checksum bailouts added. Found a correctness edge case with ZWNJ characters — added explicit detection to bail out.

2026-03-10: Load test (PerfBench) against dedicated-sim cluster at 2000rps shows 18ms median prefill latency improvement and 14% overall CPU reduction under our dev mix. Observability panels added to Console to expose bailout reasons and cache hit rate.

2026-03-12: Security/privilege review—no new sensitive data stored in cache. Confirmed KMS/HSM not impacted. Preparing canary rollout plan for next week with 5% traffic on hosted API and empty cache on Private until opt-in.
